New vs. resale

The new-build premium — apartments only

New (VEFA) means bought off-plan before completion. Comparing raw national medians is misleading: new construction concentrates in cheaper outer departments, dragging its overall average down even though it costs more everywhere it's actually built. Comparing like-for-like, department by department, tells the real story — almost entirely a story about apartments, since VEFA houses are rare in this data.

Simpson's paradox in the raw numbers: nationally, new apartments show a median of €5,711/m² against €6,846/m² for resale — a misleading −17%. Once you hold the department fixed, new apartments cost more than resale in every single department, from +6.5% in Paris up to +87% in Val-d'Oise (95).

Size effect

Price per m² falls as flats get bigger — then recovers

Small units carry a large per-m² premium everywhere (kitchens and bathrooms don't shrink proportionally, and studios serve a different, less price-sensitive buyer). The curve bottoms out around 80–100 m², then climbs again for large luxury-scale units — most sharply in the priciest arrondissements, where trophy apartments command their own premium.

Method

How this was built

Source: dvf_merged_Paris.gpkg — 2.1M raw DVF mutation records across all eight Île-de-France departments (75, 77, 78, 91–95), 2014–2025.

Sale typeKept Vente and VEFA only — dropped auctions, exchanges, expropriations (non-market prices)
GeographySingle-commune transactions only (99.9% of rows) for clean area attribution
Property scopeExactly one house or one apartment per transaction — excludes land, mixed-use, multi-lot and dependency-only sales that make €/m² ambiguous
ValidityPrice > €1,000, surface ≥ 9 m² (French legal habitable minimum)
Outliers€/m² outside €500–€30,000 removed (<1% of rows) as likely data errors
Result749,655 clean sales, 195 communes/arrondissements

All figures are medians, not means — DVF prices are heavily right-skewed by a small number of very high-value sales, and the median is far more representative of what a typical buyer actually pays.

Source: DVF (Demandes de Valeurs Foncières), French tax administration cadastral sales records, merged extract for Île-de-France, 2014–2025. Analysis and charts generated from dvf_merged_Paris.gpkg.
